Three ants walk on a thin rod 100 cm long.
When an ant reaches either end of the rod it falls off. When two ants meet,
they BOUNCE: both instantly reverse direction, and each keeps its own speed.

Starting positions and velocities (positive = toward the 100 cm end):

- Ant A: at 10 cm, moving +3 cm/s
- Ant B: at 40 cm, moving -1 cm/s
- Ant C: at 80 cm, moving -2 cm/s

After how many seconds does the LAST ant fall off the rod? Give the exact
number of seconds.


When you are finished, output your final answer on its own line, as the last line of your response, in the exact format:
ANSWER: <your answer>

text:
For this problem, we use the classic trick: when two ants collide and reverse directions, it’s equivalent to the ants passing through each other (since the ants are indistinguishable in effect). So we can treat each ant as walking straight off the rod without bouncing.

Treat the rod as spanning from 0 cm to 100 cm. Positive velocity means toward 100, negative means toward 0.

- Ant A: at 10 cm, moving +3 cm/s.
  Time to reach 100 cm: (100 − 10)/3 = 90/3 = 30 seconds.

- Ant B: at 40 cm, moving −1 cm/s.
  Time to reach 0 cm: 40/1 = 40 seconds.

- Ant C: at 80 cm, moving −2 cm/s.
  Time to reach 0 cm: 80/2 = 40 seconds.

The last ants to fall are Ant B and Ant C, both at 40 seconds.

ANSWER: 40
